title: Pappa al Pomodoro: Tuscan Tomato and Bread Soup
summary: Ripe grated tomatoes, golden garlic and basil simmered with bread until it collapses into a thick, porridge-like soup. Finished with olive oil, fresh basil and grated cheese, it is simple and full of summer flavour.
equipment: large casserole (about 5 litres) with a lid

ingredients.item: ripe tomatoes, halved across the middle
ingredients.note: about 1 litre of pulp once grated

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
fine sea salt or table salt
sprigs fresh basil, plus 2 tbsp chopped basil to serve
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated, to serve

steps.title: Grate the tomatoes
steps.text: Set the box grater in the bowl and rub the cut side of each tomato half over the large holes until only the skin remains in your hand; discard the skins. You should have about 1 litre of pulp. Grating separates the flesh from the tough skins quickly, with no need for blanching or peeling.

steps.title: Gild the garlic
steps.text: Put the oil and garlic in the casserole over medium heat and cook for 3-4 minutes, until the garlic is golden at the edges. Starting garlic in cold oil lets it flavour the oil gently without burning.

steps.title: Add tomatoes and bread
steps.text: Add the tomato pulp, salt, pepper, chilli flakes, water and basil sprigs. Tear in the bread and stir until every piece is moistened. The bread will soak up the juices and eventually melt into the soup.

steps.title: Simmer to a pappa
steps.text: Bring to the boil over high heat, then lower to medium, cover and simmer briskly for 15-18 minutes, stirring and mashing the bread now and then, until it has broken down into a thick, porridge-like soup. Covering keeps the moisture in while the bread breaks down.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and remove the basil sprigs. Spoon into bowls, drizzle with olive oil, scatter with the chopped basil and pass the cheese at the table. Serve hot, warm or at room temperature, as the flavours are just as good as it cools.

tips: This soup depends on flavourful tomatoes, so make it in summer when they are ripe and heavy for their size.
A common mistake is letting the garlic go dark brown; it turns bitter, so pull the pan off the heat if it colours too fast.
If the soup is too thick, stir in a splash of hot water; it should be spoonable, not stiff.
Choose a Parmesan made with microbial or vegetarian rennet if that matters to you, or use a vegetarian hard cheese.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days. Serve at room temperature or reheat gently with a splash of water until piping hot (74 °C). Not suitable for freezing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
